title: Should AI Engineers Still Read Code in 2026? The Z/L Continuum — Alex Volkov, ThursdAI
talk_summary: Alex Volkov frames the 'read every line vs code is free' debate as a task-level routing problem: different changes need different proof, and repeated defect classes should be pushed into linters/docs/reviewers rather than re-caught by humans. He also warns that self-grading loops hide review rather than remove it, and that separating the builder from the verifier is essential.

takeaways.technique: Route changes to the proof they need (risk-tiered review)
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a uniform review bar, classify each change by risk and route it to the matching proof: line-by-line human/agent inspection for auth, money, permissions, irreversible data; lighter checks for non-critical code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You read every line of authentication, money movement, permissions, and irreversible data.

takeaways.technique: Convert repeated defects into permanent system checks
takeaways.what_they_do: When a review catches a bug, don't just fix it — write a linter rule, doc, or reviewer instruction so that class of bug is caught automatically forever after.
Never let the same agent that writes code also write the tests and grade the output; use a distinct agent/context for verification.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you don't separate, it's kind of like if I came up with an exam and then I took an exam and I scored myself

takeaways.technique: Loops hide review rather than remove it
takeaways.what_they_do: Self-verifying loops (agent plans, executes, grades itself, retries) are useful but shift where judgment must sit; without an independent check they can spiral into deeper holes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the builder grades itself, you didn't remove the review, you hid it

takeaways.technique: Agent-driven PR decomposition into atomic reviewable units
takeaways.what_they_do: Use agents to split large changes into small atomic PRs so reviewers (human or LLM) don't glaze over huge diffs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: split it into atomic reviewable PRs. You know who's good at it? Agents.

takeaways.technique: Ask the model to flag critical code regions
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the LLM to scan a large repo and identify which files/lines are critical (auth, primitives) so attention is directed there.
